parties:
Majeda Khatun @ Majeda Rahman --------------- Petitioner
Vs.
The State ---------- Respondent.
full_judgment:
Muhammed Ansar Ali, J.: This Rule arises out of an application for bail under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure at the instance of the accused petitioner Majeda Khatun @ Majeda Rahman @ Maya in a case under sections 302/109/120B/34 of the Penal Code pending in the court of the learned Sessions Judge, Khulna. 

 2. The short facts leading to the case are as follows:- 

 4. That accordingly Daulatpur P.S. Case NO.2 dated 5.8.87 was started and on completion of the investigation the police submitted charge-sheet on 9.9.87 against this petitioner and 6 others under sections 302/109/120B/34 of the Penal Code. 

 6. This petitioner was arrested on 8.8.87 and since then she has been in the jail custody. Bail petitions on several occasions were moved on behalf of the petitioner before the learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Khulna but the same were rejected. Thereafter the petitioner moved the learned Sessions Judge, Khulna in Bail Case No. 107 of 1987 but the prayer for bail was rejected by the learned Sessions Judge by his order dated 10.1.88 with the observation that the petitioner was not named in the F.I.R. but she was named in the confessional statements of the co-accused. The petitioner again moved the learned Sessions Judge for bail in Bail Case No. 37 of 1988 stating, inter alia, that she was suffering from various fatal diseases inside the jail which require her to be treated outside the jail. The learned Sessions Judge called for a report about her health from the jail-authority, but the jail authority could not furnish a complete report as the petitioner was required to be X-rayed. The learned Sessions Judge mainly on consideration of the confessional statements of the co-accused held that the petitioner was involved in the murder of her husband and therefore, rejected her prayer for bail by an order dated 9.2.88. 

 (1) That the petitioner is innocent and she has been falsely implicated in this case at the instance of her enemies. She was not named in the F.I.R. and her name has been falsely disclosed in the so-called confessional statements of some co-accused persons who have subsequently filed petition for retraction of the same and further the statements of the witnesses under section 161 Cr.P.C. also do not show direct involvement of this accused in the killing of her husband and as such it cannot be definitely held that there are reasonable grounds to believe that the petitioner is involved in the commission of the alleged crime of murder of her husband. 

 (3) Lastly, it is submitted that in the same case one co-accused Liaqat Sharif who was not named in the F.I.R. but his involvement was subsequently alleged and disclosed in the confessional statements of some co-accused persons and in the statements of witnesses under section 161 Cr.P.C. but he has been granted bail by this court and as such this petitioner should also be granted bail having stood on similar footing. 

 10. Now, we take up for our consideration the points urged before us by the learned Advocate for the petitioner. It is true the court is generally reluctant to enlarge an accused persons on bail in a case under section 302 or 302/34 of the Penal Code. But in an appropriate case, the court can exercise the discretion in granting bail in a case for an alleged offence of murder or in any offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life. It is well settled that bail should not be withheld by way of punishment. Here in this case, it is not disputed that the petitioner is in jail custody for about 9 months without the actual trial. Admittedly, she was not named in the F.I.R. Her name was subsequently disclosed in the confessional statements of some of the co-accused persons. It is alleged that there was a previous attempt also to cause death of the victim Anisur Rahman by the present accused persons. But in spite of that the name of this petitioner was not entered in the F.I.R. leading to this case. We have carefully considered the materials placed before us and we find that only allegations of a conspiracy of the alleged murder have been made against the petitioner in the confessional statements of the co-accused and in the statements of some witnesses under section 161 Cr.P.C There is no allegation of any direct participation in causing the death of the victim on the date of occurrence made against this petitioner. So far the genuineness or the evidentiary value of the confessional statements of the co-accused and the statements of the witnesses under section 161 Cr.P.C., we are not inclined to make any comment or observation at this stage so that the parties may not be prejudiced at the time of trial of the case. 

 11. Now in this case admittedly the petitioner is a woman and the wife of the victim Anisur Rahman. It is well settled that this court has unfettered power in granting bail, but in considering a petition for bail under section 498 Cr.P.C., the guidelines as given in section 497 of the Code of Criminal Procedure should be kept in view. 

 13.	 So, it is clear that in the event of a prayer for bail on behalf of a woman, even in case of murder or in an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life, a special consideration for the accused may be made. In the instant case, it is true that the charge-sheet against this petitioner and six others has been submitted under sections 302/109/120B/34 of the Penal Code which offences are punishable with death or imprisonment for life. But still then the case of the petitioner as she is a woman deserves special consideration. Merely because the chargesheet has been submitted against her under the above sections of the Penal Code, she is not automatically debarred from gelling bail. 

 15. The last submission which has been made before us by the learned Advocate for the petitioner is that another co-accused Liaqat Sharif who is almost on similar footing in this case in the sense that he was not named in the F.I.R. but subsequently named in the confessional statements of the co-accused and the statements under section 161 Cr. P.c. has been granted bail by this Court and as such this petitioner should also be granted bail to avoid discrimination. 

 16. It is true that Liaqat Sharif was also not named in the F.I.R. but his involvement in the commission of the alleged crime was subsequently disclosed in the co-accused's confessional statements as well as in the statements of some witnesses under section 161 Cr.P.C. He has been granted bail by this Court on 13th March, 1988 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 14 of 1988. 

 17. Hence on careful consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and the materials on record, we are, however, satisfied that it is a fit case in which the petitioner should be enlarged on bail, We, however, like to mention that whatever observation we have made above, is for the limited purpose of this bail application. It must not be understood that we have decided any matter touching the merit of the case. That is ultimately for the trial Court. 

 Let the petitioner Majeda Khatun @ Majeda Rahman @ Maya be enlarged on bail to the satisfaction of the Deputy Commissioner, Khulna. It may however be made clear that the concerned court will be free to cancel the bail of the petitioner in case of any violation of the privilege of bail granted hereby to her by this Court.
